label: Impulse!
rationale: A defining late-Impulse! statement by Rollins, pairing him with Coltrane's rhythm section (Garrison-Jones) at their most telepathic. The title track is a 20-minute modal journey; Hubbard's trumpet cuts through on the opener only, adding textural contrast. Consensus core collection across Penguin Guide, DownBeat, and AllMusic. Recorded May 1966, released January 1967 on Impulse!

personnel_record.notes: Single session, May 9, 1966 at Van Gelder Studio, Englewood Cliffs (post-July 1959 move). Hubbard is on the title track only per matrix 90572. Tracks 2-3 are trio with Rollins-Garrison-Jones. Original Impulse! catalog numbers: A-9121 (mono), AS-9121 (stereo). Wikipedia also credits Rollins as co-producer alongside Thiele; AllMusic and Discogs list only Thiele.

ballot.case_for: Session gravity is the strongest signal: Rollins paired with Jimmy Garrison and Elvin Jones — Coltrane's rhythm section at its telepathic peak — in May 1966, months after the quartet dissolved, with Freddie Hubbard's verified one-track appearance (JazzDiscography matrix 90572) bridging Blue Note hard-bop lineage into the Impulse!/Coltrane orbit. It is a defining statement: Rollins' final and boldest Impulse! date before his 1969 withdrawal from recording, his most ambitious sustained modal statement of the 1960s and the most explicit Rollins–Coltrane crossover on record.
ballot.case_against: The title track's twenty minutes lean into repetitive vamps, harsh overblowing, and abrasive free-rhythmic stretches that can play as endurance test rather than cohesive composition — under John's standing free-jazz calibration, listener resonance here sharply divides. The dossier's consensus claim is asserted, not evidenced — all listed sources are catalog metadata, none is Penguin or DownBeat.
ballot.disagreement: Real split on tier — consensus_core/must_have vs contested/strong — driven by whether the modal/avant boundary is in play.
ballot.recommendation: John should listen to the full 20-minute title track before ruling: this is a contested candidate with a live modal/avant boundary question.
